data.content_ref: inline:Verisimilitude as a Regulative Ideal (SRC_005) inherits its defensive structure from Corroboration as Informational Content (SRC_006): the ideal functions only if corroboration successfully measures informational boldness without probabilistic contamination. This relation is refuted if it can be demonstrated that 'informational content' cannot be assessed independently of truth probability, forcing the regulative ideal to rely on the very inductive probabilities it claims to replace.
